We introduce DeepQuest, a knowledge-gap-driven AI scientist framework for Alzheimer's disease research. DeepQuest transforms unresolved questions from domain reviews into traceable, testable hypotheses and prioritizes them through data feasibility screening and groupwise Elo ranking. It couples iterative experimentation with two-level auditing that separates experimental reliability from knowledge contribution relative to two frozen literature corpora. On OASIS-3, DeepQuest produces 42 feasible hypotheses and outperforms the strongest baselines in 14 of 15 evaluator-dimension comparisons across three language-model reviewers. The full framework achieves an audit-assessed scientific finding rate of 95.24%, outperforming both general-purpose executors and domain-specific research agents. This scientific finding rate remains stable across literature corpora and evaluator model families. Representative findings concern neuropsychiatric symptoms and dementia risk, longitudinal amyloid spatial stability, and neocortical tau-associated clinical impairment, with key associations supported in independent ADNI and AIBL cohorts. These results show how aligning knowledge gaps, data feasibility, and evidence auditing can turn automated research into traceable, evidence-supported scientific discovery. Our source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DeepQuest-3066/

papers.title: Context as a Resource
papers.summary: Managing concurrent tasks across separate agent sessions quickly exhausts human attention, motivating always-on personal agents behind a single continuous interface. Yet when every context shares identical frozen backbone weights, funneling interleaved dialogues and external events into one linear session induces cross-topic constraint bleed and head-of-line stalling. Conversely, router-ticket hierarchies incur lossy prose handoffs, heavy routing overhead, and blind merges - collapsing true-conflict repository merges to a 33.3% three-run mean despite high isolated branch passes. Rather than scheduling anthropomorphic roles, we introduce ClonAct, a routerless architecture that virtualizes context blocks directly through a pluggable single-pass non-generative Context MMU, in-place Context Cells, a footprint-aware Synaptic Bus with an isolated trial merge gate, and a wave-flushed Shared Trunk. Across three programmatic multi-stream benchmarks and three model families, our portable trial merge gate lifts true-conflict merges to 63.3%, while ClonAct's routerless virtualization attains this ceiling with 45.9% fewer prompt tokens and prevents compact-model router collapse. Under continuous surge streams, ClonAct matches top completion (95.0%) with the lowest median wait and zero timed-out status checks.

papers.title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents
papers.summary: LLM agents on long-horizon tasks fail in recurring, procedural ways. They mis-paginate an API, resolve the wrong entity, or answer when no answer was asked. We built a pipeline that lets an agent learn from its own history. It first mines short \emph{lessons} from the agent's own trajectories, one to three per episode. It then consolidates those lessons into a smaller set of \emph{guidelines}, where each guideline records how many lessons it merged. At inference the agent receives either all guidelines or a selected subset. The pipeline ships in the open-source altk-evolve library and is deployed in IBM's CUGA agent and watsonx Orchestrate platform. We report what we learned building, measuring, and productizing it. Our primary instrument is the AppWorld benchmark, across models spanning 40--92\% baseline task completion. The central finding is that the right amount of memory is a property of the model, not the memory. A strong model keeps improving as guidelines are added. DeepSeek-V3.2 gains +9.5 points of task completion and +16.1 points of scenario completion with its full 191-guideline set. A weak model gains less from the same full set than from a small selected subset. gpt-oss-120b starts at 39.9\% task completion. It reaches 51.2\% with all 199 of its guidelines but 55.4\% (mean of two runs) with a selected subset of about 29. Around that result we report what went wrong: a high-support guideline that backfired, provenance silently dropped during consolidation, a swallowed API error that failed every task while producing a plausible log, and a baseline confound that nearly produced a misleading comparison with a prior method. We distill these into recommendations for teams deploying agent memory.

papers.title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence
papers.summary: World models are increasingly used to simulate physical interactions, but training a separate model for each environment limits scalability. Cross-environment prediction requires identifying the current physical rule, which appearance alone may not reveal. We therefore study visual calibration: using object motion and interactions in a short video as direct evidence to infer the current rule and predict motion under that rule from a different initial state. However, differences in data availability across physical conditions can yield a long-tailed training distribution, biasing models toward common rules even when evidence supports rare ones. To study this challenge, we introduce TailWorld, which evaluates the transfer of demonstrated rules across initial states while independently controlling training imbalance and calibration informativeness. The benchmark compares predictions with two reference futures from the same prediction initial state, one following the demonstrated rule and the other a common rule, to measure prediction bias toward common dynamics. We further propose Rule Inference for Transfer (RIFT), which learns how different rules affect object motion, infers the current rule from calibration interactions, and applies it to prediction from a new initial state. RIFT explicitly controls the influence of training frequency on rule inference, allowing sufficiently informative observational evidence to support rare rules. Experiments on TailWorld show that RIFT improves prediction accuracy and physical consistency across varying training imbalances and distribution shifts, with gains in predicting rare dynamics.

papers.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
papers.summary: Representative vision-language navigation (VLN) methods typically couple a vision-language model (VLM) brain with a learnable action head and fine-tune the VLM brain on navigation-domain data to predict geometric goals. However, such adaptation can substantially alter base VLM weights and degrade general visual capabilities. We introduce ZeroVLN, a slow-fast navigation framework that achieves effective navigation with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain. Rather than teaching the brain to predict geometric goals, we equip it with a semantic tool-calling interface for conveying movement decisions to an action expert in natural language. We first adapt the action expert to carry out these movement requests, then jointly improve the brain's movement decisions and the action expert's continuous execution through closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL). Trained on the same navigation episodes, ZeroVLN substantially outperforms representative SFT-based hierarchical VLN methods on standard VLN-CE (continuous environments) benchmarks, while inducing only minor changes to the brain's weights and largely preserving its general capabilities. To our knowledge, ZeroVLN is the first slow-fast VLN framework with zero navigation-domain SFT of the VLM brain, and the first to jointly optimize its slow and fast policies through closed-loop agentic RL in VLN-CE.

papers.title: Reasoning-Trace Analysis Using Large Language Models for Interpretable Q-Matrix Construction
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate Q-matrices for diagnostic classification models that approximate expert specifications, but evaluations have focused on the final matrices, leaving the basis of individual item-attribute assignments unexamined. This opacity limits the responsible use of AI in measurement. We propose Reasoning-Trace Analysis (RTA), a framework in which an LLM generates attribute-labeled reasoning steps through chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting and these steps are analyzed to reconstruct, compare, and inspect each assignment. RTA is intended to supplement expert review and empirical validation. In a simulation study with perturbed fraction subtraction items, four LLMs recovered the required attributes and withheld attributes the items did not require. In an empirical study with 11 fraction subtraction items, responses from 536 examinees, four LLMs, up to three temperatures, and 100 replications per condition, CoT-derived Q-matrices overlapped substantially with the reference Q-matrix (mean overlap .809) but less than directly generated Q-matrices (.877), and they varied more across replications. Inspection of the traces linked disagreements to item-type coding, labeling rules, and how operations were expressed as steps. Q-matrices with similar overlap differed in fit to examinee responses. RTA provides inspectable evidence that matrix-level agreement and fit do not.
papers.title_zh: 使用大语言模型的推理轨迹分析用于可解释的Q矩阵构建
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）能够为诊断分类模型生成近似专家设定的Q矩阵，但评估一直集中于最终矩阵，未考察单个题目-属性分配的依据。这种不透明性限制了AI在测量中的负责任使用。我们提出推理轨迹分析（RTA），一个框架，其中LLM通过思维链（CoT）提示生成带有属性标签的推理步骤，并分析这些步骤以重建、比较和检查每一项分配。RTA旨在补充专家审查和实证验证。在一项使用扰动分数减法题目的模拟研究中，四个LLM找回了必需属性，并未赋予题目不需要的属性。在一项实证研究中，包含11个分数减法题目、536名考生的作答、四个LLM、最多三个温度以及每种条件100次重复，CoT导出的Q矩阵与参考Q矩阵有实质性重叠（平均重叠 .809），但低于直接生成的Q矩阵（.877），且它们在重复之间变化更大。对轨迹的检查将分歧与题目类型编码、标注规则以及操作如何表示为步骤联系起来。具有相似重叠度的Q矩阵在对考生作答的拟合上存在差异。RTA提供了矩阵层面的一致性和拟合所不能提供的可检查证据。

papers.title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models
papers.summary: Deep-research agents repeatedly decide what to search, read, and verify, often using large cloud-hosted language models for action proposal. However, privacy and local control motivate running agents on users' devices, where limited memory and compute favor smaller models and complicate on-device training. Yet inference-time guidance faces three obstacles: exploring alternatives through real execution adds tool calls, prompted self-evaluation is bounded by the agent's judgment, and model-specific guidance risks repeated adaptation costs. We introduce Seer, an inference-time framework providing local guidance that separates the agent's action proposal from learned consequence prediction and value estimation. From a shared corpus of real research trajectories, we train two models: a tool-response simulator on observed call--response pairs and a value estimator on histories labeled with discounted terminal correctness. The simulator and estimator are trained offline and reused across agents without further training. Moreover, Seer executes only the selected action and adds only real tool responses to the committed history, avoiding tool calls on discarded candidates at additional inference cost. Across multiple deep-research benchmarks, Seer substantially improves agent performance for different language models. For instance, GAIA accuracy rises from 13.6% to 41.7% for Qwen3.5-4B and from 22.3% to 50.5% for Qwen3.5-9B. Furthermore, our analyses suggest that broader candidate coverage can compensate for imperfect simulation, while prediction and scoring errors limit the benefits of wider imagined search. These findings highlight the potential of reusable models for prediction and evaluation to strengthen small research agents through extra local computation without the real execution of the discarded candidates.

papers.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
papers.summary: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid ($>250\times$ dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width extension ($d \to d+K$) with $\sqrt{d/(d+K)}$ norm compensation, Base-1000 canonical BPE emission, and differential $(+254,-256)$ tied unembeddings. An automated 5-stage compiler synthesizes 4-8 digit signed $\{+,-,\times\}$ circuits in constant $\mathsf{TC}^0$ depth alongside 3-literal Boolean (100%, $N=1{,}728$; plus 42-layer Gemma 4 E4B audits) and 5-bit Majority/Parity (100%) circuits. On 6-digit arithmetic ($N=1{,}200$, BF16), IBM Granite 4.2 3B (1.07M-1.33M active non-zeros, $\le 0.036\%$) and Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B (2.25M-2.39M non-zeros, $\le 0.057\%$) reach 99.17% and 100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy (100% with an FP32 sidecar) and 98%-100% mid-sentence resumption, outperforming 12.8K-sample LoRA (42.2% / 61.7%, 0% inline continuation). A factorized block-sparse sidecar holds A100 memory at 7.89 / 10.65 GiB (4.60 / 8.14 GiB under INT8/INT4 + FP32 sidecar) while passing all 14/14 pre-registered $>2$K-token Tango splits ($N=4{,}392$; 0/11,134 OOD triggers).

papers.title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces
papers.summary: Set pieces produce about a third of non-penalty expected goals (xG), yet they are usually evaluated by what happened next. We present Monte Carlo Pass Search (MCPS) for set pieces, which treats a corner or a lofted free kick as a distribution over plausible executions and plausible futures instead of a single realised event. From the pre-kick state, MCPS proposes counterfactual deliveries and counterfactual set-ups (where the attackers stand at the kick), plays each out many times in a world model (3D ball physics, a generative model of all 22 players, the keeper's come-or-stay decision and a Player-to-Touch model) and scores every future with a value model. On 249 deliveries from 30 Serie A 2025/26 matches, with every model applied only to matches it never saw, the best available delivery is worth 0.0085 xG more than the one kicked (+28 %), mainly because it reaches an attacker before the keeper. Searching where the attackers stand as well adds +0.0027 xG with the observed ball and +0.0033 on top of the best ball; designing their runs too adds +0.0007 more. We show how to keep such a search honest, and estimate how much more data each component needs before a club could rely on it.

papers.title: FLUID: Flexible, Evidence-Grounded Situated Task Guidance
papers.summary: Real-time task guidance is inherently flexible: when an agent guides a user through a task, multiple responses and timings can be appropriate, and sometimes the best action is to remain silent. Existing benchmarks often miss this flexibility by treating synthesized dialogues as fixed targets for what to say and when to say it. We introduce FLUID (Flexible, Evidence-Grounded Situated Task Guidance), a unified framework for modeling, evaluating, and enabling flexible interaction in multimodal task guidance. Using naturally occurring human-human guidance from WTaG and HoloAssist, FLUID grounds interventions in their supporting evidence, necessity, and timing flexibility, and uses this representation both to evaluate flexible guidance and to build a real-time agent for task guidance. Our agent achieves the strongest overall balance of response correctness, intervention precision, timely guidance, and response latency among evaluated systems, while still leaving room for improvement in avoiding speech overlap. Together, FLUID moves situated task guidance beyond rigid reference matching toward more natural and adaptive human-AI interaction. Project page: https://fluid-guidance.github.io.

papers.title: GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers
papers.summary: Decision models enable fast, confidence-aware decisions by scoring candidate answers in a single forward pass, without generating text or intermediate reasoning. Yet reasoning can substantially improve decision quality, raising the question of whether its benefits can be retained without the cost of generating it. We investigate this question with \textbf{GLiDE}, a family of decision models spanning 0.4B to 27B parameters. Building on Qwen hybrid language models, GLiDE enables bidirectional interactions between the context, question, and candidate answers by removing causal masking from full-attention layers. To transfer reasoning capabilities into single-pass inference, we combine soft-target distillation from multiple teachers, including a reasoning model, with progressive post-training on diverse decision tasks. We further explore parameter-free recurrent depth to increase inference-time computation without generating tokens. Across five model sizes, GLiDE lies on the performance--parameter Pareto frontier of the Hugging Face \DI{}, with each model outperforming evaluated alternatives of equal or smaller size. \dmtwo{} (27B) achieves a hidden-set score of 71.52, with an expected calibration error of 2.0\% and a median latency of 92.9\,ms on a single GPU. Further checkpoint averaging and parameter-free recurrent depth yield GLiDE~27B, which reaches 73.37 with an expected calibration error of 2.1\%.

papers.title: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits
papers.summary: Intersectional bias arises when a model treats people who hold several marginalised identities at once differently from what their separate identities would predict. Auditing such intersectional subgroups remains a challenge: their number grows quadratically, and there is no agreed baseline for what independent attributes would predict. Without such a baseline, many existing audits flag a subgroup when it exceeds each attribute alone, a condition that attributes acting independently already satisfy. We test this standard criterion on 150 synthetic datasets built with no interaction. With the shuffle null, it flags 66.1 false subgroups per dataset on average, and at least one in every dataset. When we plant interactions of known size into these datasets, a repaired null lets the criterion recover only 32% of them. We introduce ADDIS (Additive Intersectional Screen), which fits an additive model over all attributes, scores each subgroup by its Additive Residual Distance (ARD) from that model's prediction, and tests it against a Freedman-Lane null. On our synthetic benchmark, ADDIS flags 0.09 false subgroups per dataset and recovers 84% of the same planted interactions. We then build IndiPersona, 10,000 synthetic Indian personas with six identity attributes, and audit 13 open language models. The standard criterion flags 7.1% of the 738 tested subgroups on average; ADDIS flags 3.0%. Gender identity crossed with sexual orientation is the largest pairing in every model, and counterfactual personas confirm it and additionally reveal a caste x class interaction in all but one model that the observational test lacked the data to detect. Much of what audits report as intersectional bias can thus arise from independent single-attribute effects alone, yet a small core of interactions survives.

papers.title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Linear probes are the cheapest LLM lie detectors but often fail to transfer across kinds of lie. Label-free directions from honest and deceptive role-play are untested at 70B scale and on lies about knowledge, where a lie and an honest denial can be identical. We widen a published persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they have, plus honest counterparts. At each model's middle layer the resulting persona direction ranks lies across Liars' Bench better than single-dataset probes on three of its four models; it fails on Qwen, even when Qwen stays in role far more often. On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct it beats directions from a random persona bank, but its gain over the published direction is within the range of random widenings. On lies about knowledge, persona directions mainly track a reply's wording: where lies and honest denials share their words, our three main contrasts stay inside the random-direction band on Llama and Qwen and reach only its edge on Gemma, though on Mistral one clears it. A knowledge direction contrasts questions the model can answer with ones nobody can, each followed by the same scripted denial. It separates lies from identical honest denials on two models and narrowly on a third, but not on the fourth; its other results partly depend on the benchmark's wording. On the Gender-Secret fine-tune it clears the band by a few hundredths on Llama and fails on Mistral. The sum of the two directions ranks lies better than a supervised probe at the same depth on all four models (on one, both near chance) but is level with the persona direction on Llama's average and behind that probe on held-out lies. More varied role-play questions do not help the persona direction on Liars' Bench.
papers.title_zh: 谎言的几何：用于检测大语言模型欺骗的知识方向与人格方向
papers.abstract_zh: 线性探针是最便宜的大语言模型谎言检测器，但往往无法在不同类型的谎言之间迁移。来自诚实与欺骗性角色扮演的无标签方向在70B规模上以及关于知识的谎言上尚未经过检验，而在关于知识的谎言中，谎言与诚实否认可能完全相同。我们扩展了一个已发表的人格库，加入否认自己拥有知识的角色，以及诚实的对应角色。在每个模型的中间层，所得人格方向在Liars' Bench上对谎言进行排序，在四个模型中的三个上优于单数据集探针；它在Qwen上失败，即使Qwen更常保持角色。在Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct上，它优于来自随机人格库的方向，但其相对于已发表方向的增益处于随机扩展的范围内。在关于知识的谎言上，人格方向主要追踪回复的措辞：当谎言与诚实否认用词相同时，我们的三个主要对比在Llama和Qwen上仍位于随机方向带内，在Gemma上仅达到其边缘，尽管在Mistral上其中一个越过了它。一个知识方向将模型能够回答的问题与无人能够回答的问题进行对比，每个问题后都跟随相同的脚本化否认。它在两个模型上以及勉强在第三个模型上将谎言与完全相同的诚实否认区分开，但在第四个模型上不能；它的其他结果部分取决于基准的措辞。在Gender-Secret微调上，它在Llama上以几个百分之一的幅度越过该带，而在Mistral上失败。两个方向之和在全部四个模型上对谎言的排序优于同一深度的监督探针（在其中一个模型上，两者都接近随机水平），但在Llama的平均值上与人格方向持平，并在留出谎言上落后于该探针。更多样的角色扮演问题无助于人格方向在Liars' Bench上的表现。

papers.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
papers.summary: When multimodal decision models determine actions, moderation outcomes, or quality judgments, their reliability depends on preserving semantic decisions across presentation changes, ignoring irrelevant additions, and distinguishing information consistent with task evidence from information that conflicts with it. Existing evaluations study decision-interface biases and multimodal model behavior in separate settings, leaving no common protocol to compare multimodal decision models with their backbones on practical tasks. We introduce \textbf{MM-SystemOneBias}, which evaluates 13 models on 5,323 original instances from nine public datasets and 11 task scenarios using six paired interventions: option order, option label, external judgment, image--text description, irrelevant information, and rating scale. Across seven matched decision-model--backbone pairs, decision models are more stable under option-label, irrelevant-information, and rating-scale changes in all seven pairs; six pairs also show lower option-order flip rates. They incur smaller accuracy losses under incorrect external judgments in all seven pairs and conflicting descriptions in six. In six pairs, they gain less accuracy from correct external judgments and show less favorable accuracy changes under consistent descriptions. Among pairs with unchanged semantic decisions, mean absolute changes in answer probabilities range from 4.56 to 11.55 percentage points, revealing input effects that accuracy alone misses.

papers.title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
papers.summary: Graphic designs are ordered compositions of RGBA layers whose separation enables selection, movement, and reuse. Existing layered models represent each layer with a full-canvas or region-sized spatial latent grid, so representation size grows with the cumulative spatial extent of the layers. We present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework built on ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder that encodes a design into one shared spatial prototype and one candidate vector per layer. Each candidate conditions a shared decoder to reconstruct its corresponding RGBA layer. For $N$ layers, the representation contains $HW+N$ tokens before backbone-specific packing, compared with $NHW$ for full-grid-per-layer representations. ProtoDiffusion jointly denoises the prototype and a fixed set of candidate slots, conditioned on an image or text, with bounding boxes as optional layout guidance. The model leaves unneeded slots empty and determines the number of layers and, in absence of boxes, their layout, requiring neither as input. The same architecture supports both image-to-design and text-to-design. ProtoVAE achieves high-fidelity reconstruction from its compact shared latent representation, reaching 40.43 dB PSNR on layer crops. On the LayerD evaluation split, image-to-design achieves RGB L1 scores of 0.040 with bounding boxes and 0.057 without, with box-guided alpha soft IoU (0.850) comparable to the strongest fine-tuned baseline (0.871). On merged images, text-to-design reaches 66.41 FID versus 86.84 for FLUX.2 [klein], achieves a 0.860 text-accuracy score, and runs $19.1\times$ faster than the same-backbone generation-then-decomposition cascade.
papers.title_zh: ProtoDiffusion：多层图像的逐层Token生成建模
papers.abstract_zh: 图形设计是由 RGBA 层组成的有序组合，这些层的分离使得选择、移动和复用成为可能。现有的分层模型用全画布或区域大小的空间潜在网格表示每一层，因此表示大小随各层累积的空间范围而增长。我们提出 ProtoDiffusion，一个构建于 ProtoVAE 之上的潜在扩散框架，ProtoVAE 是一种多层变分自编码器，可将一个设计编码为一个共享空间原型以及每层一个候选向量。每个候选向量对共享解码器进行条件化，以重建其对应的 RGBA 层。对于 $N$ 层，在进入骨干网络特定的打包之前，表示包含 $HW+N$ 个 token，而每层全网格表示则为 $NHW$ 个。ProtoDiffusion 以图像或文本为条件，联合对原型和一组固定的候选槽进行去噪，并以边界框作为可选的布局引导。该模型将不需要的槽留空，并确定层数以及在没有边界框时确定这些层的布局，而这两者都不需要作为输入。同一架构同时支持图像到设计和文本到设计。ProtoVAE 从其紧凑的共享潜在表示实现高保真重建，在层裁剪图像上达到 40.43 dB PSNR。在 LayerD 评估划分上，图像到设计在有边界框时取得 0.040 的 RGB L1 分数，无边界框时为 0.057，其中边界框引导的 alpha soft IoU（0.850）与最强的微调基线（0.871）相当。在合并图像上，文本到设计达到 66.41 FID，而 FLUX.2 [klein] 为 86.84，取得 0.860 的文本准确率分数，并且运行速度比同骨干的先生成后分解级联快 $19.1\times$。

papers.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computation. (i) Accessibility and selective access. Multimodal concept information is readable in intermediate states and selectively accessible as tasks require. We extend "readout carriers" from one name token to a token set to better capture and express concept information and support counterfactual experiments. (ii) Concepts in downstream computation. Counterfactual experiments show that accessed concept information participates in downstream computation and reasoning. (iii) Development of cross-modal alignment and selective access. We develop two J-space metrics tracking the development of cross-modal concept alignment more clearly than hidden state cosine in controlled VLM training. The experiment also shows that reliable selective access develops later than concept accessibility. (iv) Shared functions across models. Across VLM families and sizes, we find shared patterns of concept accessibility, query-dependent selectivity and cross-task intervention effects despite differences in internal organisation. These findings offer an experimental basis to study GWT in multimodal artificial systems and how it can guide cross-modal alignment improvements.

papers.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
papers.summary: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.

papers.title: CAIMS: Scalable Cross-Array In-Memory Search
papers.summary: Search, especially top-k similarity search, plays a vital role in many applications, but its performance can be severely limited by memory access overhead. In-memory search (IMS), an alternative to CPU/GPU-based approaches, exploits massive parallelism within a content-addressable memory (CAM) array to perform search in situ and provides both low latency and high energy efficiency. However, the capacity of a single CAM array is often insufficient for modern workloads, requiring data to be distributed across multiple arrays. Deploying scalable top-k similarity search across multiple CAM arrays poses a fundamental problem that existing designs fail to address: how to accurately and efficiently reduce local binary match results to global top-k results. This work introduces CAIMS, a cross-array IMS framework that is agnostic to memory technologies and applications, enabling scalable and efficient top-k similarity search while preserving accuracy. To enable accurate top-k result reduction, CAIMS leverages the existing threshold match functionality with a combined offline and online parameter selection approach to transform local binary match results that lack globally comparable similarity information into global coarse-grained similarity scores. To further improve efficiency, CAIMS conducts hierarchical reduction and transfers only the selection results and necessary control signals with lightweight local peripherals. Implemented on a 3D NAND Flash model and demonstrated using the retrieval phase of retrieval-augmented generation, CAIMS improves throughput by up to $22.3\times/10.1\times$ and energy efficiency by $426.6\times/23.7\times$ compared to the server-class CPU baseline and prior 3D NAND Flash accelerators, respectively, while maintaining comparable accuracy.

papers.title: Native FPGA Hard-Block Implementation from High-Level Synthesis
papers.summary: High-level synthesis (HLS) maps computations to FPGA hard blocks, yet often leaves their arithmetic modes, internal registers, and cascade links idle and recreates them in the fabric, costing area and timing. We present a C++ template library that reaches native hard-block implementations without modifying the HLS compiler. Templates fix source patterns, and an automatic flow picks scheduling settings and verified RTL patches. On AMD Versal, our matrix multiplication uses 2.4--4.5x fewer lookup tables (LUTs) than AutoSA systolic arrays at equal or higher estimated throughput. Our INT8 matrix--vector units reach the three multiply--accumulates per DSP of hand-written FINN RTL, versus at most 1.29 for HLS libraries. In hls4ml, Allo, and Stream-HLS, the templates cut LUTs by up to 2.7x and DSPs by up to 2x.

papers.title: Bottom-Up FPGA Reconfigurable Accelerator Overlay Generation
papers.summary: Programmable FPGA overlays run new workloads without re-synthesis, yet they pay twice. An overlay adds a second layer of programmability on top of the FPGA's own overhead. Moreover, overlay generators usually start from a regular template, so they spend logic on switches and links that the workloads never use, and they close timing at low clocks. We present a flow that instead grows an overlay bottom-up from the dataflow graphs of the workloads it must run. The flow clusters workloads by structural similarity, ranks shared slots with spectral descriptors of each operation's surroundings, and adds only the units and links a workload lacks. It builds every unit on native hard blocks, with their internal pipeline registers, dual-ported memories and double-pumped DSPs, and it uses fixed-function engines where wider data types exceed the overlay's 16-bit lanes. Workloads then switch by configuration alone. On an AMD VCK5000, across 17 workloads from three suites and against OverGen rebuilt for the same board, our images run at 250-400 MHz instead of 35-50 MHz. As a result, they are 9.52-10.33x faster in geometric mean, and up to 36.97x, while using 19.4-22.1x less of the FPGA and 9.67-10.51x less estimated board energy.

papers.title: RE-CAM: Readout-Enhanced Content-Addressable Memory for Quantitative Similarity Search
papers.summary: Similarity search is essential to many applications but incurs massive data movement when executed on conventional architectures. Content-addressable memory (CAM) is a promising hardware substrate, as it allows similarity search directly in the CAM array, minimizing data movement and offering both low latency and high energy efficiency. However, conventional CAM array readout produces only binary match results, discarding quantitative similarity information that could be further exploited. Extracting this information requires interpreting the CAM array output voltage that evolves during a CAM search, making the sensing timestamp a crucial design variable alongside the reference voltage and decoding parameter. In this work, we propose RE-CAM, a readout enhancement framework for CAM that is agnostic to memory technology and application, enabling CAM array readout to approximate linear and nonlinear functions with one CAM search. By reusing the comparators to sense the time-varying output voltage multiple times, jointly optimizing the three design variables under system constraints and hardware nonidealities, and co-designing the optimization algorithm and reconfigurable hardware, RE-CAM achieves accurate approximation with low energy and area overhead without introducing a readout throughput bottleneck. Across linear, piecewise-linear, sigmoid, and exponential functions, RE-CAM reduces normalized root mean square error by 10.89% to 24.34% for general approximation and 29.43% to 46.73% when exploiting dataset distribution, compared to a shared uniform-reference ADC baseline with the same comparison budget. Relative to the same baseline, RE-CAM also achieves $8\times$ higher search throughput while reducing energy per search and area by 47% and 39%, respectively.

papers.title: ReLay: Bidirectional Layout-Code Translation and Library Evolution for Reusable and Process-Portable Analog Design
papers.summary: Analog layout generators provide a programmable interface for design reuse and process migration, but their coverage is limited by handcrafted libraries. The designer knowledge embedded in complete layouts remains implicit in their geometry, making it difficult to capture in reusable generator libraries. We present ReLay, a bidirectional layout-code framework that recovers generator programs from existing layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs. Constructions that recur across recovered programs are promoted to library functions, so the library evolves as layouts accumulate. We also introduce the first layout-code benchmark: 1,050 hand-drawn layouts from 27 circuit families across three open-source PDKs, ranging from primitive cells to full chips. Learned functions account for 53-66% of layout-building calls in held-out layouts, demonstrating reuse beyond the learning corpus. Frontier LLM agents use ReLay to produce new layouts at 64-77% lower API cost per completed task than direct geometry generation, with comparable completion rates and electrical quality.

papers.title: FPGA-GEN: Target-Aware RTL Generation via HLS
papers.summary: Successful C/C++ compilation does not guarantee correct or efficient FPGA hardware after high-level synthesis (HLS). FPGA-GEN is an agentic HLS-C generation workflow that encodes specification, readiness, selection, repair, and admission rules in explicit task contracts and bounded tool-feedback loops for candidate-level decisions. On HLS-Eval, five shared-context outputs per task yield 407/425 (95.8%) public-testbench passes. In a cumulative conversion campaign, FPGA-GEN admits 104/107 (97.2%) HLS-LeVeri designs under held-out co-simulation, Vivado synthesis/fit, and same-RTL evidence. In focused TensorCore screening, selected candidate 3 reports 73.7% fewer CSynth cycles and 14.6% fewer LUTs than generated/composed C0, with 26.7% more DSPs, and passes development CoSim.

papers.title: SGLayout: Schema-Guided Closed-Loop Refinement for LLM-Driven Parameterized Layout Generation
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential in parameterized layout generation via tool-augmented code synthesis. However, LLMs lack spatial awareness, making one-shot generation unreliable. While layout quality can be evaluated with established techniques, a critical gap remains: geometric-domain evaluation outcomes cannot be directly translated into actionable code-level fixes, trapping iterative refinement in blind refactoring. We propose SGLayout, a self-refining framework that closes this gap via a schema-guided mechanism. Upon code execution, a structured schema captures the correspondence between each code-level instance and its geometric attributes, establishing a bidirectional link between code space and geometry space. Emulating engineer review practices, SGLayout evaluates layouts along two complementary dimensions: intent compliance through quantitative structural checking and qualitative vision-language assessment, and rule compliance through DRC. All identified violations are then back-projected through the schema onto precise code targets, enabling surgical repair. This closed-loop process iterates until layout convergence. On a curated benchmark of 112 parameterized layout generation tasks using GDSFactory, SGLayout achieves a 76.79% pass rate, compared with 50.89% for the strongest baseline.
papers.title_zh: SGLayout：模式引导的闭环精化，用于LLM驱动的参数化版图生成
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）已通过工具增强的代码合成在参数化版图生成中展现出强大潜力。然而，LLMs缺乏空间感知能力，使得一次性生成并不可靠。尽管可以使用已有技术评估版图质量，但仍存在一个关键缺口：几何域评估结果无法直接转化为可操作的代码级修复，从而使迭代精化陷入盲目重构。我们提出SGLayout，一个通过模式引导机制弥合这一缺口的自精化框架。在代码执行时，结构化模式捕获每个代码级实例与其几何属性之间的对应关系，建立代码空间与几何空间之间的双向链接。SGLayout模拟工程师评审实践，沿两个互补维度评估版图：通过定量结构检查和定性视觉-语言评估来评估意图符合性，并通过DRC评估规则符合性。随后，所有识别出的违规都通过该模式反向投影到精确的代码目标上，从而实现精准修复。该闭环过程迭代进行，直至版图收敛。在一个使用GDSFactory的112个参数化版图生成任务的精选基准上，SGLayout达到76.79%的通过率，而最强基线为50.89%。

papers.title: BOOMerang: Autonomous Translation from RTL to Microarchitectural Simulators and Back
papers.summary: High-level simulators like gem5 are often used to test and demonstrate novel architectural techniques. While these simulators provide high research productivity, they generally lack the means to provide detailed feedback on the realizability of a hardware design. Furthermore, these simulators can frequently fall out-of-sync with the detailed performance characteristics of real hardware designs, which is usually the responsibility of dedicated engineers/teams in industry. While RTL implementation can address these challenges, it can be even more difficult to translate simulator code to high-quality RTL by hand without a large team. In this work, we architect and evaluate agentic loops that automate both parts of the RTL vs. high-level simulator workflow that is critical to high-quality architecture research. Our loops (1) automatically generate accurate high-level models of RTL implementations of CPU designs (BOOM) in a battle-tested microarchitecture simulation framework (gem5) and (2) automatically translate new microarchitectural features implemented in the high-level simulator back to RTL faithfully. Targeting the first loop at autonomously building a gem5 model for the Berkeley Out-of-Order Machine (BOOM) core, we generate a simulator with IPC within 3% of the RTL, meeting targets pursued for simulators in industry, in only 2 days. We use our second loop to automatically translate 72 features from this aligned gem5 simulator into RTL in the BOOM core, while maintaining its low IPC error. Combining translated optimizations together yields a 25% performance improvement for the BOOM core RTL implementation in SPECint 2017, demonstrating that having these loops for moving between high-level simulation and RTL enables actual improvement of processor performance. The agentic loops we developed and the simulators and RTL we generated will be available in open-source.

papers.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
papers.summary: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. However, realizing this opportunity requires scaling experience banks, introducing substantial storage and search overhead that challenges the capacity, bandwidth, and power constraints of edge systems. We propose FlashX, a CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA)-based NAND flash architecture for scalable experience reuse in embodied agents. FlashX exploits CBA's high internal bandwidth for parallel pSLC key search, employing interleaved Compute-in-Flash (CIF) engines to sustain sensing throughput while retaining dense TLC latent storage. Proprioception-aware clustering further reduces search overhead and enables incremental experience acquisition without global reclustering. Evaluations across VLA and WAM workloads demonstrate up to 12.24\%p and 7.43\%p improvements in task success under dense and compute-efficient configurations, respectively. FlashX achieves 2.57$\times$ higher search throughput than the strongest prior NAND search architecture under pSLC sensing, with a further 9.7$\times$ search reduction through clustering. This delivers 1.29--3.95$\times$ end-to-end speedup and 1.12--2.34$\times$ energy efficiency improvement over SSD-based retrieval.
papers.title_zh: FlashX：利用基于 CBA 的 NAND Flash 扩展具身智能体的机器人经验复用
papers.abstract_zh: 具身智能体正成为复杂机器人任务的一种有前景的范式，其利用视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型和世界动作模型（WAMs），通过基于扩散 Transformer（DiT）的迭代去噪来生成动作。然而，现有模型往往难以泛化到分布外（OOD）环境。我们观察到，检索成功的经验并用其热启动去噪，能使智能体更好地适应不熟悉的情境，同时降低计算开销。这创造了一个同时提升任务准确率和推理效率的新机会，与以精度换取计算的传统加速技术形成对比。然而，实现这一机会需要扩展经验库，这会引入大量的存储和搜索开销，对边缘系统的容量、带宽和功耗约束构成挑战。我们提出 FlashX，一种基于 CMOS 直接键合到阵列（CBA）的 NAND 闪存架构，用于具身智能体中的可扩展经验复用。FlashX 利用 CBA 的高内部带宽进行并行 pSLC 键搜索，采用交错的闪存内计算（CIF）引擎来维持感测吞吐量，同时保留密集的 TLC 潜在存储。本体感受感知聚类进一步降低搜索开销，并实现无需全局重新聚类的增量经验获取。在 VLA 和 WAM 工作负载上的评估表明，在密集配置和计算高效配置下，任务成功率分别最高提升 12.24\%p 和 7.43\%p。在 pSLC 感测下，FlashX 的搜索吞吐量比此前最强的 NAND 搜索架构高 2.57$\times$，并通过聚类进一步实现 9.7$\times$ 的搜索缩减。相较于基于 SSD 的检索，这带来了 1.29--3.95$\times$ 的端到端加速和 1.12--2.34$\times$ 的能效提升。

papers.title: Splice-Core: Low-Order-Bit-Splicing GEMM for Highly Energy-Efficient AI Inference Accelerators
papers.summary: Splice-Core is a temporal-unary/binary (tub) hybrid general matrix multiplication (GEMM) unit that minimizes low-order accumulation latency, while retaining value-dependent execution for high-order activation bits. We present two novel processing element (PE) variants: (i) Splice-BP utilizing bit planes, and (ii) Splice-LUT, which selects a shared weight multiple in a single cycle. Compared to a binary systolic array, Splice-BP/Splice-LUT achieve 77.4%/76.4% geometric-mean tile energy reductions, respectively, across 26 INT4 convolutional neural network (CNN) and large language model (LLM) workloads in 45nm. Splice-LUT further increases geometric-mean tile throughput by 44.4% and reduces geometric-mean energy-delay product (EDP) by 6.13x across the 26 configurations. Across the evaluated W8A8 convolution and expert-projection workloads, Splice-BP and Splice-LUT reduce tile energy by 77.3-88.1%. Post-place-and-route INT4 yields 14%/9% smaller area for Splice-BP/Splice-LUT, compared to the systolic array.
papers.title_zh: Splice-Core：面向高能效 AI 推理加速器的低阶位拼接 GEMM
papers.abstract_zh: Splice-Core 是一种时序一元/二进制（tub）混合通用矩阵乘法（GEMM）单元，它最小化低阶累加延迟，同时保留针对高阶激活位的值相关执行。我们提出了两种新颖的处理单元（PE）变体：（i）利用位平面的 Splice-BP，以及（ii）Splice-LUT，它在单个周期内选择一个共享权重倍数。与二进制脉动阵列相比，Splice-BP/Splice-LUT 在 45nm 工艺下的 26 个 INT4 卷积神经网络（CNN）与大语言模型（LLM）工作负载上，分别实现了 77.4%/76.4% 的几何平均瓦片能耗降低。Splice-LUT 进一步在 26 种配置上将几何平均瓦片吞吐量提高 44.4%，并将几何平均能量延迟积（EDP）降低 6.13 倍。在所评估的 W8A8 卷积与专家投影工作负载上，Splice-BP 和 Splice-LUT 将瓦片能耗降低了 77.3-88.1%。布局布线后的 INT4 结果显示，与脉动阵列相比，Splice-BP/Splice-LUT 的面积分别小 14%/9%。

papers.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
papers.summary: Large Language Models show great potential for automated Register-Transfer Level repair, yet they struggle with non-local faults where root causes and failing outputs reside far apart in source code. Treating RTL as a flat token sequence obscures hardware dataflows, whereas exposing complete synthesized graphs overwhelms the model with fine-grained metadata. To resolve this representation dilemma, we propose GRODE-RTL, an anchor-centric representation that extracts the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register from the netlist, maps netlist nodes back to editable source lines, and organizes them into a compact hop-partitioned dependency view. By prioritizing direct drivers and folding distant hops, GRODE-RTL guides standard tool-using agents without exposing ground-truth hints or oracle feedback. We evaluate GRODE-RTL across 30 formally validated non-local faults using three LLMs (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2, and MiniMax-M3) alongside a controlled six-configuration ablation study. GRODE-RTL improves pass@1 over source-level exploration by 16.7% on DeepSeek, by 26.7% on GLM-5.2, and by 20.0% on MiniMax-M3, with consistent gains on the hard-to-retrieve far-distance and indirect-anchor subsets of all three models. Our controls isolate structural relevance from generic context expansion, proving that selective dependency organization rather than full graph exposure is key to effective RTL repair.
papers.title_zh: GRODE-RTL：面向基于LLM的RTL修复的源码映射依赖视图
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型在自动化寄存器传输级修复方面展现出巨大潜力，但在非局部故障中表现不佳，此类故障的根本原因与失败输出在源代码中相距很远。将RTL视为扁平令牌序列会掩盖硬件数据流，而暴露完整综合图则会以细粒度元数据使模型不堪重负。为解决这一表示困境，我们提出GRODE-RTL，一种以锚点为中心的表示，它从网表中提取可疑寄存器的单时钟级扇入锥，将网表节点映射回可编辑的源代码行，并将它们组织成紧凑的按跳数分区的依赖视图。通过优先处理直接驱动源并折叠远距离跳，GRODE-RTL指导标准的使用工具的智能体，而不暴露真实答案提示或预言机反馈。我们使用三个LLM（DeepSeek-V4-Flash、GLM-5.2和MiniMax-M3）在30个经过形式验证的非局部故障上评估GRODE-RTL，并进行一项受控的六配置消融研究。与源码级探索相比，GRODE-RTL在DeepSeek上将pass@1提高了16.7%，在GLM-5.2上提高了26.7%，在MiniMax-M3上提高了20.0%，并且在所有三个模型的难以检索的远距离和间接锚点子集上均取得一致增益。我们的对照实验将结构相关性与通用上下文扩展隔离开来，证明选择性依赖组织而非完整图暴露是有效RTL修复的关键。

papers.title: Mitigating Row Buffer Contention Through Multiple Row Buffer (MRB) DRAM
papers.summary: DRAM chips contain multiple banks to handle sev- eral memory requests in parallel. However, requests to different rows of the same bank (e.g., from different cores or workload access patterns) interfere with each other by contending for a single shared row buffer. This introduces row buffer conflicts, which incur performance and energy overheads. In this work, we reduce row buffer conflicts caused by interference by introducing multiple row buffers in each bank. We propose multiple row buffer (MRB) DRAM, which employs a primary global row buffer along with multiple secondary SRAM row buffers in the DRAM chip. These secondary SRAM row buffers act as a cache that enables each bank to serve requests to multiple rows in parallel, thereby improving performance and reducing row buffer conflicts. Our evaluation shows that MRB-DRAM with four SRBs per bank improves performance by an average of 29.7%, 24% in singlecore, multicore systems, respectively, compared to a conventional DDR4 baseline with a modest area overhead of 2%.

papers.title: CRAFT: Analog Circuit Design by Reasoning LLM Agents from Pre-Computed Lookup Tables
papers.summary: Automated analog circuit sizing methods, from black-box optimizers to recent large language model (LLM) agents, typically search the design space with a SPICE simulator in the loop, whereas an experienced designer works out a design by hand analysis. This paper presents CRAFT, a flow in which an LLM agent designs a given topology by calculation, as a designer does, and without an initial sizing. The agent works only through DeX, a service that uses pre-computed lookup tables to provide device characteristics and to solve the whole netlist for its operating point and small-signal response. It thus designs without SPICE, and every final design is verified independently in HSPICE. We test CRAFT on four circuits in a commercial 28 nm process; the largest is a 37-transistor three-stage amplifier with 53 design variables, 20 specifications and 74 saturation constraints. With Claude Opus 5.5, CRAFT meets every specification and constraint in all 20 runs, five per circuit. On that amplifier, with DeX in place of HSPICE and an identical request for both, the same agent passes in 10 of 10 runs instead of 6 of 10 within an hour and is 2.0x faster at the median.
papers.title_zh: CRAFT：推理型 LLM 智能体基于预计算查找表的模拟电路设计
papers.abstract_zh: 自动模拟电路尺寸设计方法，从黑箱优化器到近期的大型语言模型（LLM）智能体，通常都在回路中借助 SPICE 仿真器搜索设计空间，而经验丰富的设计者则通过手工分析完成设计。本文提出 CRAFT，这是一种流程，其中 LLM 智能体像设计者一样通过计算来设计给定拓扑，并且无需初始尺寸设计。该智能体仅通过 DeX 工作，DeX 是一项服务，它使用预计算查找表提供器件特性，并求解整个网表的工作点与小信号响应。因此它在不使用 SPICE 的情况下完成设计，并且每个最终设计都在 HSPICE 中独立验证。我们在商用 28 nm 工艺中的四个电路上测试 CRAFT；最大的是一个 37 个晶体管的三级放大器，具有 53 个设计变量、20 项规格和 74 个饱和约束。使用 Claude Opus 5.5，CRAFT 在全部 20 次运行（每个电路五次）中满足每一项规格和约束。在该放大器上，当用 DeX 替代 HSPICE 且对两者提出相同请求时，同一智能体在一小时内 10 次运行中通过 10 次，而不是 10 次中通过 6 次，并且在中位数上快 2.0 倍。

papers.title: Kameleo: In-Situ Activation-Precision Selection for Bit-Serial LLM Accelerators
papers.summary: Weight-only quantization keeps the activations of large language models (LLMs) in a higher-precision format, pushing the on-chip inference cost to the activation arithmetic. Bit-serial, variable-length accelerators offer a promising path to reduce this cost by lowering activation precision while preserving model quality. They process only the mantissa bits that each layer needs. The length has to be chosen per layer and operator, and today it is chosen by offline calibration: a search driven by the perplexity of the full model on a representative dataset. The search is repeated for every model and workload, and its result degrades silently on other data. This paper presents Kameleo, an accelerator that selects the activation precision at runtime, on the accelerator, from the data it is processing. Kameleo replaces the global perplexity by a local proxy that compares the output of each GEMM at reduced and at full precision. It exploits the fact that a bit-serial datapath produces this comparison almost for free, because the reduced-precision result is an intermediate state of the full-precision computation. Two passes over the first tokens of a workload set the precision of every GEMM. On four LLMs and seven datasets, Kameleo stays within a 1% perplexity budget at a 2.11-2.34x reduction of prefill cycles on the matrix multiplication unit (MXU), close to the reduction of configurations calibrated offline on the evaluation data itself. Calibrated configurations transferred to other data, in contrast, often violate the budget. The selection hardware adds only 3.7% to the accelerator area. Kameleo thereby makes variable-length mantissas feasible in real deployments, where offline calibration for every model and workload is not.
papers.title_zh: Kameleo：面向位串行 LLM 加速器的原位激活精度选择
papers.abstract_zh: 仅权重量化使大语言模型（LLM）的激活保持为更高精度的格式，从而将片上推理开销推向激活算术。位串行、可变长度加速器通过降低激活精度同时保持模型质量，为降低这一开销提供了一条有前景的路径。它们仅处理每一层所需的尾数位。该长度必须按层和算子分别选择，而目前它是通过离线校准来选择的：一种由完整模型在代表性数据集上的困惑度所驱动的搜索。该搜索对每个模型和工作负载都要重复进行，且其结果在其他数据上会悄然退化。本文提出 Kameleo，一种在运行时、在加速器上、根据其正在处理的数据来选择激活精度的加速器。Kameleo 用一个局部代理替代全局困惑度，该局部代理比较每个 GEMM 在降精度和全精度下的输出。它利用了这样一个事实：位串行数据通路几乎可以免费地产生这种比较，因为降精度结果是全精度计算的中间状态。对工作负载的首批 token 进行两遍处理，即可设定每个 GEMM 的精度。在四个 LLM 和七个数据集上，Kameleo 在 1% 的困惑度预算内，将矩阵乘法单元（MXU）上的预填充周期减少 2.11–2.34 倍，接近在评估数据本身上离线校准的配置所达到的减少幅度。相比之下，迁移到其他数据上的校准配置常常会超出该预算。选择硬件仅使加速器面积增加 3.7%。因此，Kameleo 使可变长度尾数在实际部署中变得可行，而在这些部署中，为每个模型和工作负载进行离线校准并不可行。

papers.title: Scalable fault vulnerability analysis for ReRAM-based process-in-memory CNN accelerators
papers.summary: Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM)-based processing-in-memory (PIM) accelerators offer a highly efficient platform for parallel matrix-vector multiplications (VMM) in neural networks, leveraging analog computation, high density, low leakage, and non-volatility. However, their susceptibility to permanent faults, such as stuck-at-high (\textit{SaH}) and stuck-at-low (\textit{SaL}) resistance states, permanently corrupts the convolutional neural networks (CNNs) weights mapped onto ReRAM cell conductance values, thereby degrading inference accuracy and leading to system unreliability in safety-critical applications. Fault injection is a commonly used technique to assess the vulnerability of neural networks by systematically injecting faults into individual parameters and measuring the resulting accuracy degradation. Although this method is accurate, it is prohibitively time-consuming and computationally expensive, especially for large-scale CNNs. In this paper, we propose a fast, scalable, and analytical framework to quantify the fault vulnerability of convolutional neural networks deployed on ReRAM-based PIM accelerators. This method quantifies vulnerability at different granularities, including weights, kernels, and layers, without the need for exhaustive simulation, enabling the design of fault-tolerant accelerators for edge and safety-critical applications. The comparison between the results of the proposed vulnerability score (VS) metrics with performance metric of CNNs captured with fault injection simulations confirms the effectiveness of our proposed method. Unlike exhaustive fault injection, which requires days or weeks, whereas the proposed approach achieves a speedup of about $10^4\times-10^5\times$, enabling fast and accurate vulnerability analysis for large-scale CNNs within only a few minutes or hours.

papers.title: MaskPE: One Mask, Two Roles: Weight Placement and MAC Gating in Systolic Arrays
papers.summary: Unstructured pruning reduces weight storage but does not inherently reduce execution cost in conventional weight-stationary systolic arrays. Packed nonzero weights must be restored to fixed processing-element positions, while zero-weight positions must preserve data forwarding. This paper presents MaskPE, a mask-directed systolic architecture that uses positional masks to steer nonzero weights during preload and clock-gate arithmetic registers in zero-weight processing elements during execution, reducing dynamic power while preserving systolic dataflow. At 50% sparsity, MaskPE reduces compressed weight storage by 34.9%, including metadata overhead. RTL validation confirms exact execution with no additional steady-state tile stalls, while gate-level simulations demonstrate 12.5--14.4% lower execution energy across samples of seven LLM projections.

papers.title: FoldSim: Scaling Cycle-Exact RTL Simulation with Hierarchical Folding and Static Scheduling
papers.summary: RTL simulation is essential for hardware design and verification, yet its execution time grows rapidly with design scale and complexity. CPU- and GPU-based simulators exploit parallelism to accelerate RTL evaluation, but achieving high simulation throughput for large designs remains challenging. FPGA-based simulators offer higher throughput by mapping RTL computations directly onto hardware, but their scalability is constrained by FPGA resource capacity. We present FoldSim, an automated framework that enables cycle-exact simulation of large RTL designs on a single FPGA through hierarchical folding. FoldSim maps instances across the design hierarchy onto shared logic while maintaining their independent state. Given foldable module classes, its compiler constructs a static schedule that coordinates their execution, reducing dynamic synchronization overhead and making state accesses predictable. FoldSim backs state that exceeds on-chip capacity with external memory and brings it to the shared circuits as needed. A configurable DRAM model separates target-memory timing from host delays. The compiler explores replica allocations and state placement to balance resource savings against simulation time. On one AMD Alveo V80, FoldSim runs an 8-SM GPU and a 1,024-node Rocket datacenter with 4,096 processor cores. The unfolded implementations require approximately 16x and 200x as many LUTs as FoldSim's, respectively. The datacenter keeps about 1.9 GB of state in HBM, while a 4-SM GPU completes a 1024x1024 GEMM in 4.24 seconds, versus 26 hours in software RTL simulation.

papers.title: From Seed to BLOOM: Autonomously Growing a Better Out-of-Order Core
papers.summary: Improving microprocessor performance while meeting ASIC implementation constraints like area and frequency is a complex and labor-intensive task that requires expertise across computer architecture, hardware design, and performance analysis and profiling. While large teams in industry can afford the engineering resources to target this problem across performance modeling, RTL design, and ASIC implementations, small teams of researchers and engineers cannot take on this huge engineering burden while keeping up with the pace of advancement in processor microarchitecture. Recent advancements in large language model (LLM) agents present a promising substrate to accelerate this traditionally human-intensive process. In this work, we build and evaluate MiracleGro, an agentic AI-based system that, without human intervention, analyzes cycle-level RTL behavior and synthesis results, identifies performance bottlenecks, and translates architectural ideas into RTL implementation in a leading open-source out-of-order superscalar application core, the Berkeley Out-of-Order Machine (BOOM). Taking into account cycle-exact performance, area, and critical path, MiracleGro automatically produces improved BOOM designs that drastically increase the human-optimized BOOM's performance on substantial workload suites such as SPEC CPU2017 with full reference inputs. MiracleGro achieves an 85% IPC speedup and a frequency improvement of 27% in SkyWater 130nm, resulting in a 2.34x wall-clock time speedup on the full SPEC CPU2017 intspeed benchmarks (30 trillion instructions). This result demonstrates the enormous opportunity to harness frontier models to improve state-of-the-art RTL-driven platforms for implementation-grounded microarchitecture research across hardware designs.
papers.title_zh: 从 Seed 到 BLOOM：自主生长出更好的乱序核心
papers.abstract_zh: 在满足面积和频率等 ASIC 实现约束的同时提升微处理器性能，是一项复杂且劳动密集的任务，需要横跨计算机体系结构、硬件设计以及性能分析与剖析的专业知识。尽管业界的大型团队能够负担工程资源，从性能建模、RTL 设计和 ASIC 实现等方面来解决这一问题，但小型研究人员和工程师团队无法在跟上处理器微体系结构发展步伐的同时承担这一巨大的工程负担。大型语言模型（LLM）智能体的最新进展为加速这一传统上人力密集的过程提供了一种有前景的基础。在这项工作中，我们构建并评估了 MiracleGro，这是一个基于智能体 AI 的系统，无需人工干预即可分析周期级 RTL 行为和综合结果、识别性能瓶颈，并将体系结构思想转化为领先的开源乱序超标量应用核心——伯克利乱序机（BOOM）中的 RTL 实现。在考虑周期精确的性能、面积和关键路径的情况下，MiracleGro 自动生成改进的 BOOM 设计，在诸如使用完整参考输入的 SPEC CPU2017 等大规模工作负载套件上大幅提升人类优化后的 BOOM 的性能。MiracleGro 在 SkyWater 130nm 上实现了 85% 的 IPC 加速和 27% 的频率提升，从而在完整的 SPEC CPU2017 intspeed 基准测试（30 万亿条指令）上实现了 2.34 倍的实际运行时间加速。这一结果展示了巨大的机会：利用前沿模型改进最先进的由 RTL 驱动的平台，以开展跨硬件设计的、基于实现的微体系结构研究。

papers.title: Fundamentals for Binary Classification Under Label Noise
papers.summary: This chapter surveys fundamental results for binary classification under label noise. Binary classification under label noise involves training models on datasets where class labels are partially incorrect, leading to degraded performance and misclassification. We distinguish poisoning attacks from noise processes and formalize random classification noise, Massart noise, and malicious classification noise within the probably approximately correct (PAC) framework. These models capture different adversarial strengths and data-generation realities. We then highlight some core ideas and representative results. In particular, we explain why random classification noise preserves the expected ordering of hypotheses and thus supports learning using the empirical risk minimization (ERM) principle, how sample complexity depends on the noise rate, and why learning algorithms often require an upper bound on the corruption level, as well as how such a bound may be estimated from data in the case of random classification noise. We also discuss computational aspects of ERM under noise and present a canonical negative result technique -- the method of induced distributions -- within the malicious noise model where the adversary has more power and may affect not only the label of an example but also the instance. We conclude with pointers to related work and a taxonomy that organizes classical label-noise models using the NCAR/NAR/NNAR lens.

papers.title: Products of Distinguisher Hulls
papers.summary: The distinguisher hull of two distributions is the convex hull of the pairs of acceptance probabilities of tests in a specified class. We study its behavior under independent products for size-bounded Boolean circuits. We derive a geometric consequence of Dwork and Tankala's supersimulator theorem (FOCS 2026), giving a substantially different proof of approximate product containment for distinguisher hulls. In particular, our construction uses nonadaptive sampling in place of adaptive score corrections.

papers.title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)
papers.summary: The global deployment of autonomous AI agents within and across organisations exceeds the governance infrastructure available to constrain it. Agent communication and authentication protocols, principally the Model Context Protocol and the Agent2Agent Protocol, are maturing quickly, but maturity at the protocol layer does not produce legal legibility at the governance layer. Runtime enforcement written by the deploying organisation fixes the resources an AI agent can reach, not the authority under which it acts. Legal legibility is the capacity of a legal system to recognise, interpret and regulate activity by mapping it onto legal personhood, property, rights and liabilities. Existing (analogue) legal infrastructure cannot supply it for autonomous deployment. The resulting deficit is bidirectional. It concerns the attribution of liability when an AI agent causes harm, and the allocation of rights, including data and economic rights, generated by agentic activity and by the AI agent itself as a source of value and form of property. This paper characterises that deficit as the legal attribution gap, a material and unaddressed risk to economies, organisations and citizens that is magnified in cross-organisational multi-agent deployment. The paper describes the Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA), in which AI systems and data assets are registered as legal objects anchored to one or more identified legal persons, governed by cryptographically tethered smart legal instruments and evaluated at runtime. Each smart legal instrument can carry a legal context clause, through which the legislation, regulation and judicial decisions in force at the time of the act are given practical and legal effect in that evaluation. Infrastructure of this kind is a precondition for the continued function of any legal, property and economic system with both human and autonomous machine stakeholders.

papers.title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) write fluent financial analyses but miscompute ratios, recall stale prices, and route questions to the wrong tool with high confidence. We ask which component should do each job in a financial question-answering assistant, and study it with FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent research prototype over SEC filings and live market data: a compact typed-decision model (Laya) routes each question and screens out advice requests, Python computes every number, retrieval and tools fetch evidence, Mistral-7B writes a cited answer, a code validator checks that cited IDs exist and that numbers match computed notes, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes the pipeline. In live experiments, Laya routed better than Mistral-7B (0.85 vs. 0.52; overall 0.86 vs. 0.68, McNemar p = 0.0003); a 12B Mistral decided no better, and DeepSeek-R1-8B decided better (0.79 vs. 0.68, p = 0.0192) but about 9.9 times more slowly. Mistral-7B computed 29% of 100 financial calculations correctly against 100% for Python, a live quote cut price error from 210% to 0.00%, and hybrid retrieval reached 76% Hit@5 on 50 filing questions. Yet in a live case study, both agent answers passed validation while describing AMD sample data under NVIDIA's and Alphabet's names. A controlled upper-bound study on the FinRank benchmark explains why: when one figure in the shared evidence is corrupted, self-consistency stays confident (agreement 0.55 to 0.59 while accuracy falls from 0.50 to 0.00), and a shared-evidence check (the kind our validator performs) catches 35% of the errors, whereas a check against the original passage catches 77% ($p = 5.96 \times 10^{-8}$); for DeepSeek-R1-8B, 68% vs. 90%. Verification must be independent of the evidence the writer saw.
papers.title_zh: FinVeriQA：用于问答的金融研究智能体：路由、检索、MCP 工具使用与来源感知的证据验证
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）能写出流畅的金融分析，却会错误计算比率、回忆过时价格，并以高置信度将问题路由到错误的工具。我们追问在金融问答助手中每个任务应由哪个组件完成，并用 FinVeriQA 加以研究；FinVeriQA 是一个基于 SEC 文件和实时市场数据的开源多智能体研究原型：一个紧凑的类型化决策模型（Laya）对每个问题进行路由并筛除建议类请求，Python 计算每一个数字，检索与工具获取证据，Mistral-7B 撰写带引用的答案，一个代码验证器检查被引用的 ID 是否存在以及数字是否与计算笔记匹配，而一个 Model Context Protocol（MCP）服务器暴露该流水线。在实时实验中，Laya 的路由表现优于 Mistral-7B（0.85 对 0.52；总体 0.86 对 0.68，McNemar p = 0.0003）；一个 12B 的 Mistral 决策并不更好，而 DeepSeek-R1-8B 决策更好（0.79 对 0.68，p = 0.0192），但速度约慢 9.9 倍。Mistral-7B 在 100 项金融计算中正确计算了 29%，而 Python 为 100%；实时报价将价格误差从 210% 降至 0.00%；混合检索在 50 个申报文件问题上达到 76% 的 Hit@5。然而在一项实时案例研究中，两个智能体的答案都通过了验证，却将 AMD 的样本数据冠以 NVIDIA 和 Alphabet 的名称进行描述。一项在 FinRank 基准上的受控上限研究解释了原因：当共享证据中的一个数字被破坏时，自洽性仍保持自信（一致性为 0.55 到 0.59，而准确率从 0.50 降至 0.00），共享证据检查（我们的验证器执行的那种）捕获 35% 的错误，而对照原始段落的检查捕获 77%（$p = 5.96 \times 10^{-8}$）；对于 DeepSeek-R1-8B，这两个比例分别为 68% 与 90%。验证必须独立于撰写者所见的证据。

papers.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.summary: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. However, these methods can introduce lossy compression, potentially discarding details needed for future tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce GrepMem, a simple, lossless, and index-free memory mechanism built on two components: an append-only plain-text log of the agent's complete history and a regular-expression search tool for on-demand recall. Unlike structured memory systems, GrepMem requires no embeddings, retrieval index, memory extraction, or additional models. We train Qwen3.5-9B with reinforcement learning under five context management strategies and evaluate on multi-question research sessions, long-stream recall, and agent-trajectory question answering. GrepMem achieves 95-97% accuracy on ContextBench, versus at most 21% for lossy baselines, and outperforms SUPO's summarization by 8.8 percentage points on BCP-Multi. GrepMem scales effectively to increasingly long input streams while remaining on the accuracy-token-cost Pareto frontier across all five evaluation tasks. Our results show that a plain-text log and grep provide a simple but competitive approach to long-horizon agent memory, without requiring complex structured memory infrastructure.

papers.title: Blind Spots Travel, Knowledge Stays Home: What RL Inherits from an LLM Judge
papers.summary: LLM judges serve as rewards where no answer key exists, in the hope that their knowledge passes to the trained model. In 814 RL runs that teach 7-8B models to answer closed-book questions or abstain, we ask what passes. What a grader knows about single answers stays home. A wrong answer that a judge rewards is memorised for that one question. A model trained with the answer key, or with a far stronger judge, chooses which new questions to answer no better than the untrained model does by sampling 32 answers and abstaining where they disagree; the grader's knowledge adds about one corrected answer per hundred questions. What a grader believes about a kind of question travels. A judge that rejects eleven of the twelve correct training answers about capitals of former states teaches the model to refuse 98% of such capitals on new questions, a loss that accuracy and abstention rates do not reveal. Changing only those twelve verdicts by hand moves the refusal from 5% to 90%, even for a grader that accepts as many answers as the answer key; at that leniency, two of four judges already cost 38-42% of these capitals. The capitals are not forgotten: with "I don't know" blocked, the model answers 94% of them correctly. The grader therefore needs no knowledge of its own: rewarding the model for giving the answer that most of its own untrained samples agree on, with no labels and no judge, earns the answer key's reward and keeps the category.

papers.title: When Objectives and Evaluators Disagree: Evaluating Transfer for Post-hoc Demographic Framing Mitigation
papers.summary: Post-hoc rewriting is used to reduce demographic disparities in LLM-generated text when the source model is inaccessible. A rewrite can look successful merely because it improved its own target or satisfied its selector. We study this as a transfer problem on 660 gender pairs and 1,980 age contrasts of demographic-conditioned climate messages. A rewriter proposes edits, a selection model chooses among constraint-satisfying candidates, and an independent evaluator uninvolved in either rates pairwise framing disparity. A fixed policy that always targets the message with the lower Persuasion Bias Index (PBI) transfers inconsistently across axes and outcome aggregations. An adaptive policy that proposes edits on both sides but accepts at most one significantly improves on that rule, applied to the same candidates, in seven of eight comparisons across two evaluator families, mostly by editing more pairs, not by guided direction choice, at higher preservation risk. A policy editing both messages gives the largest point reductions on fewer pairs. These two policies reduce disparity across a preservation-threshold sweep; absolute ratings vary across evaluator families and prompts. Shrinking the PBI gap increases dimension-mean disparity under both evaluator families. Mitigation should be reported as transfer across objectives, evaluators and their prompts, and editing policies.

papers.title: LLMs Are Already Confidence-Aware Zero-Shot Classifiers
papers.summary: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation). We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (1B-32B parameters) on five classification datasets with 3 to 151 labels, measuring classification performance (accuracy, F1-macro), discrimination (AUROC), and calibration (ECE and Brier score). The choice of confidence method rarely impacts accuracy significantly, but logit-based scoring methods lead to much better discrimination (AUROC 0.74-0.77) than black-box methods (AUROC 0.57-0.66). Replacing labels with single-token identifiers preserves discrimination but costs 3-6 accuracy points on average. We also introduce decision-only scoring, which only scores positions where labels diverge in the prefix tree (trie). It reduces decode steps by 88-96% on the three largest label sets and performs comparably to full-label scoring. The best open-weight model-method configurations (Gemma 4 31B and Qwen 3.5 9B) are competitive with the commercial Jev 1.13.0 classifier.
papers.title_zh: LLMs 已经是置信度感知的零样本分类器
papers.abstract_zh: 零样本大语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地被用作文本分类器，但只有当我们知道能在多大程度上信任它们时，它们的标签才有用。我们比较了黑盒方法（言语化置信度和采样）与读取 token 概率的白盒方法（P(True)，以及使用约束生成的多种 logit 评分方法）。我们在五个包含 3 到 151 个标签的分类数据集上评估了十一个开放权重 LLM（1B–32B 参数），测量分类性能（准确率、F1-macro）、区分能力（AUROC）和校准性（ECE 与 Brier 分数）。置信度方法的选择很少显著影响准确率，但基于 logit 的评分方法带来的区分能力（AUROC 0.74–0.77）远好于黑盒方法（AUROC 0.57–0.66）。用单 token 标识符替换标签可以保持区分能力，但平均会损失 3–6 个准确率百分点。我们还引入了仅决策评分，它只对标签在前缀树（trie）中发生分歧的位置进行评分。它在三个最大的标签集上将解码步骤减少了 88–96%，并且性能与全标签评分相当。最佳开放权重模型-方法配置（Gemma 4 31B 和 Qwen 3.5 9B）与商业 Jev 1.13.0 分类器具有竞争力。

papers.title: Enhancing Understanding of Language Models with Varied Explanations
papers.summary: Language models are increasingly used to support human judgement in complex reasoning tasks, yet their predictions often remain difficult to interpret and validate. Explainability techniques provide insight into model decision-making, helping expose errors, failure modes, and potential bias so users can decide whether to rely on model outputs. Explanations are simplified approximations of a language model's internal workings. The goal is to obtain explanations that reflect the underlying computation as closely as possible (faithfulness), are understandable to users (plausibility), and help them achieve their intended goals (utility). Evaluation protocols are essential for assessing these dimensions. This thesis studies highlight explanations, natural language explanations, and chain-of-thought reasoning. These forms offer complementary perspectives on model behaviour and exhibit distinct strengths and limitations across tasks. Producing explanations that satisfy multiple quality dimensions remains challenging, as does evaluating them reliably across forms and settings. This thesis aims to improve people's understanding of models' decision-making processes in complex reasoning tasks. First, it proposes two evaluation frameworks for assessing highlight explanations across multiple properties and explanation types, together with a meta-evaluation framework for examining the reliability of existing faithfulness metrics for chain-of-thought explanations. Second, it proposes two techniques that generate natural language explanations designed to be faithful to the model's prediction process while remaining concise, coherent, and helpful for understanding model decisions. Finally, a study of human-AI interaction explores the roles of evidence and explanations in helping users validate model verdicts in a fact-checking setting.

papers.title: Incorporating argumentation frameworks for LLM decision-making: Task-specific design and evaluation
papers.summary: Argumentation frameworks (AFs) provide explicit, formal mechanisms for representing and resolving conflicts and thus have been incorporated into large language model (LLM) decision-making. The benefits vary and depend on how arguments and their relations are constructed, evaluated, and incorporated into the decision process. {We abstract a workflow consisting of four stages based on existing argumentation-augmented methods} and investigate their design choices over tasks of debate-based decision-making and retrieval-based fact verification. Our evaluation with recent LLMs shows that existing methods do not consistently improve performance across the considered tasks. Motivated by this observation, we develop two task-specific methods. The first is called Qnt-Arg, which organizes arguments around the original speakers in debate materials and aggregates model-estimated argument strengths and candidate-answer priors under gradual semantics. The second is Qlt-Arg that uses credibility estimates to establish preferences between conflicting evidence items and applies grounded semantics to select acceptable evidence for subsequent LLM inference. We examine the roles of generative and decision models within the two methods. In the debate setting, Qnt-Arg consistently outperforms other argumentation-augmented methods across matched configurations; Qlt-Arg improves retrieval-based fact-verification performance compared with the baselines. These findings demonstrate the value of combining formal argumentation and LLM while highlighting the importance of aligning with tasks in argumentation construction, model selection, and the role of formal semantic reasoning.
papers.title_zh: 将论证框架纳入LLM决策：任务特定的设计与评估
papers.abstract_zh: 论证框架（AFs）提供了用于表示和解决冲突的显式、形式化机制，因此已被纳入大语言模型（LLM）决策中。其收益各不相同，并取决于论证及其关系如何被构建、评估以及纳入决策过程。我们基于现有的论证增强方法抽象出一个由四个阶段组成的工作流，并考察其在基于辩论的决策和基于检索的事实核查任务上的设计选择。我们使用近期LLM进行的评估表明，现有方法在所考虑的任务上并不能持续提升性能。受此观察启发，我们开发了两种任务特定的方法。第一种称为Qnt-Arg，它围绕辩论材料中的原始发言者组织论证，并在渐进语义下聚合模型估计的论证强度和候选答案先验。第二种是Qlt-Arg，它使用可信度估计在相互冲突的证据项之间建立偏好，并应用grounded语义来选择可接受的证据以供后续LLM推理。我们考察了生成模型和决策模型在这两种方法中的作用。在辩论设置中，Qnt-Arg在匹配配置下始终优于其他论证增强方法；与基线相比，Qlt-Arg提升了基于检索的事实核查性能。这些发现证明了将形式化论证与LLM相结合的价值，同时强调了在论证构建、模型选择以及形式语义推理的作用方面与任务保持一致的重要性。

papers.title: ChronoDossier: Long-Form Personas as Temporal Memory Representations
papers.summary: Long-horizon agents rely on stored records to recover a person's state as facts change. Reliable answers depend on how facts are recorded, retrieved, and presented to the reader. We treat a long-form persona dossier as a memory representation of a known latent state, an invariant identity plus a timeline of facts, routines, and decision rules tied to life phases.
